title: How to Prevent Dirty Background and Flying Foil

seo.title: How to Prevent Dirty Background and Flying Foil

content:
Dirty background and flying foil happen when metallic marks appear outside the intended stamped design. This problem is especially visible on clean white boxes, cosmetic packaging and luxury gift boxes.

## Common Causes

The process setting may be too strong. Excessive temperature, too much machine force or long contact time can make the foil transfer beyond the intended edge. A foil grade that releases too easily may also create unwanted marks around fine details.

Static and cleanliness are also important. Dust on the paper, foil path or stamping plate can create random metallic specks. Dry environments may increase static and make small foil particles more noticeable.

## How to Reduce the Problem

Start by reducing temperature slightly. If the background becomes cleaner, the original setting was too strong. If the issue remains, reduce machine force and check whether the foil grade is too easy-release for the artwork.

Clean the machine path, paper surface and stamping plate before testing. Store foil rolls in stable conditions and keep them protected from dust.

## FAQ

### Is flying foil always a material problem?

No. It can come from process settings, static, dust or foil release behavior.

### Why does it happen more in dry weather?

Dry air can increase static, which makes small foil particles easier to attract.

## Sample Support

Send photos of the background marks and your current settings. We can suggest process changes or a cleaner-release foil grade.
